newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes higher vs US dollar on rebound.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes higher vs US dollar on rebound.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2962 on Thursday from a 1997 low of 8.2990 on Wednesday against the U.S. dollar on a technical rebound, dealers said.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2966.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2965 and consolidated in a narrow range between 8.2960 and 8.2965 for most of the session, hitting an intraday low of 8.2968 and a high of 8.2950.
Trading was active, with most done at about 8.2965, traders said. Dealers said profit-taking emerged to push the yuan up after falls in the past few days.
"The rebound was expected as the yuan has fallen too much in the past two days," one dealer said.
"The news that two foreign banks started yuan business today also helped the currency's rebound," a second dealer said.
The Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation and Japan Industrial Bank began local currency business on Thursday in Shanghai's economic development zone of Pudong.
The dealer said this had strengthened expectations that demand for the local currency would rise and help the yuan's upward trend in the short term.
Dealers expected the yuan to move steadily between 8.2960 and 8.2970 on Friday.
The yuan closed little changed at 6.7002 from 6.7000 against 100 Japanese yen and up at an intraday high of 1.0700 from 1.0713 against the Hong Kong dollar.
